name: Malcolm Soto
life: “I set tables for strangers while my first marriage turned into notes on the fridge.” Friday often includes a stop at the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms, where Malcolm prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I thought the pencil insults were aimed at me. Now I'm meeting the reader who was arguing with a fictional husband.
appearance: Malcolm has a crooked front tooth visible when laughing. Look for brown hair pinned away from the temples. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a cream pullover with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. In conversation Malcolm draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first.
personality: Malcolm has a long memory for unfair prices and a short one for small insults. Malcolm can get along perfectly well with an enemy provided the account between them is clear.
agenda: To read the notes with the person who lived through the same disappointment.
family: June Brady is Malcolm’s older cousin. Malcolm saves a place. June chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The crash anniversary*, June says, “I bought the cheapest flowers every Friday.”
connections: Nell Marks. A blunt translation establishes who the old insults actually addressed.

reactions.situation: A reader asks to erase a personal inscription
reactions.response: Malcolm puts a clean sheet over the inscription while its writer decides.

reactions.situation: An envelope of wages is found under a café chair
reactions.response: Malcolm asks the cashier to hold it and lets a claimant identify the writing and amount privately.

reactions.response: Malcolm agrees on an amount both can bear losing before any cash changes hands.
